messages.content:
The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: io-shop requests failed with errors
Why, in plain words: The cause is not known.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 13s {duration}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Nothing was done to end it.

Name {duration} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
io-shop requests failed with errors
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: onset unknown, alerted Nov 12, 2026, 12:52:57 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 12:54:06 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 12:52:59 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 12, 2026, 12:53:10 UTC - insufficient evidence

Summary
No onset was measured; the alert came at 12:52:57 UTC. The service was not back to normal by 12:53:10 UTC, at least 13 seconds after the alert. No loss was estimated: no onset was measured to count it from. The cause is not known. Argus handed the incident to a person. io-shop could keep failing requests with no person paged to see it.

Impact
at least 13s - since the alert, still not back to normal
not measured by the metrics - peak error rate
not counted by the metrics - requests failed
not estimated - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
Not determined: the investigation named no cause.
Causal chain
symptom io-shop requests failed: the HighErrorRate alert reported its error rate above threshold. No metrics, logs or change events that Argus read show why, so the evidence stops here.
  Evidence:
    AL1 Error rate above threshold for 5m
Contributing factors
- The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not routed to anyone on call. No on-call incident was linked, so nobody was paged. (AI-2)
- Argus could not read io-shop's per-minute metrics. The query came back with 0 minutes (T4), so no onset, error rate or trend could be measured. (AI-3, AI-5)
- No io-shop log lines came back for the period before the alert. Both queries returned nothing (T8, T16). (AI-4, AI-5)
- The platform reported no pods for io-shop (T6), but the rollout read shows 3 replicas running (T12). Argus could not see where the replicas run. (AI-6)
- The deployment history does not name the revision the io-shop replicas run (T12). (AI-7)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The evidence does not identify a cause. Metrics returned no minutes, logs were empty for 11:30 UTC to 12:52:57 UTC, no pods were reported, and no changes were recorded since 2026-11-01. The rollout has converged. A dependency failure or a monitoring gap are possible but nothing supports either. I would need metrics or logs covering the period, or pod placement. | - | never tried

Trigger
No trigger was established.

Resolution
Nothing was done to end it.

Detection
The onset is unknown. HighErrorRate fired at 12:52:57 UTC - its rule fires only once its condition has held for 5 minutes.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Have a member of io-shop's owning team check io-shop's current error rate directly and find the cause of the failure, since the incident was escalated with no cause found. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-2 | Route the HighErrorRate alert for io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Fix the metrics source so that Argus can read io-shop's per-minute metrics. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Fix log collection so that io-shop's log lines reach the store Argus queries. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Add an alert that fires when io-shop's metrics or log lines stop arriving. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Make io-shop's pod placement visible to Argus so that the platform's pod listing matches the replicas the rollout reports. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Record the revision name in io-shop's deployment history for every rollout. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- 10 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 11 days 12 hours 52 minutes 57 seconds before Nov 12 12:52:57.
- 13 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus moved the incident to ESCALATED - insufficient evidence.
What went wrong
Nothing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)
 | Nov 12 12:52:57 | DETECTED | HighErrorRate on io-shop fired
T1 | 12:52:59 |  | Argus Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
T2 | 12:53:01 |  | Argus Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
T3 | 12:53:02 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 12:52:57
T4 | 12:53:02 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 0 minutes of metrics
T5 | 12:53:02 |  | Investigator Agent Looked from 12:52, the minute the alarm fired in - nothing dates when the incident began
T6 | 12:53:02 |  | Investigator Agent Recorded where the service's replicas run - the platform reported no pods
T7 | 12:53:05 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's log lines, the 30 minutes 57 seconds before 12:52:57
T8 | 12:53:05 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 0 log lines
T9 | 12:53:05 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 57 seconds before Nov 12 12:52:57
T10 | 12:53:05 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 0 production changes
T11 | 12:53:05 |  | Investigator Agent Read the service register - the service calls io-pricing (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-summary-cache (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-pay (third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd)
T12 | 12:53:05 |  | Investigator Agent Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
T13 | 12:53:07 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 11 days 12 hours 52 minutes 57 seconds before Nov 12 12:52:57
T14 | 12:53:08 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 0 production changes
T15 | 12:53:08 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's log lines, the 52 minutes before 12:22
T16 | 12:53:08 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 0 log lines
T17 | 12:53:10 |  | Investigator Agent Formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1
T18 | 12:53:10 |  | Investigator Agent Read every channel available
T19 | 12:53:10 |  | Argus Read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 12:53:10
T20 | 12:53:10 |  | Argus Moved the incident to ESCALATED - insufficient evidence

Response effort
none - engineer time
47,114 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/5ff5f274-c1ae-4ac3-9681-54dc268609c0
Changes to production read
Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
Read; none came back.
Assumptions
- No loss estimate: no minute of the service's metrics could be read, so there is no measured incident to attribute a loss to
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
○ Key incident data collected (for a person)
  no minute of metrics came back for the incident window; collecting them is for a person
✗ Impact assessed (not met)
  no loss was estimated; the service was never seen back to normal
✗ Root-cause analysis complete (not met)
  the causal chain stops at the symptom; no candidate was confirmed - none was tried; the chain does not reach a cause
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: Some requests to io-shop failed with errors, and the incident lasted {duration}. The record gives no estimate of what this cost the business. The cause is not known. No on-call responder was paged, because no on-call incident was linked to this one. Nothing was done to end the incident.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.

tools.name: judge_claims
